Add `--cors` for browser clients; `--host 0.0.0.0` is opt-in.

engines.NAME: mflux
engines.WHAT: A line-by-line MLX port of a dozen image model families, written from scratch rather than wrapping diffusers - FLUX.2, Z-Image, Qwen Image, Krea 2, Ideogram 4, FIBO and more, plus SeedVR2 for upscaling and Depth Pro for depth. It is deliberately minimal and explicit, and it is the most active image runtime on Apple Silicon by a distance. There is no server: you drive it from the CLI or import it, so putting it behind an API is your job.

engines.NAME: MLX-Audio
engines.WHAT: The centre of gravity for audio on Apple Silicon, and the largest catalogue on this page: twenty-odd TTS families, a similar spread of speech-to-text, speaker diarisation, speech enhancement and music generation. If an audio model has an MLX port at all, this is usually where it lives.

engines.NAME: MLX-Video
engines.WHAT: Inference and finetuning for image, video and audio generation models. Same author as MLX-Audio. Worth checking the commit history before planning around it - it moves in bursts rather than continuously.

engines.NAME: DiffusionKit
engines.WHAT: Argmax's on-device image generation for Apple Silicon, covering both MLX and Core ML. Solid engineering, but it has not been touched since April 2025, so it predates every model added to this page and should be treated as a reference implementation rather than a live option.

useCases.LABEL: Agentic & tool use
useCases.AXIS: Tool-use and agent benchmarks. Scores are from different suites - they justify each placement rather than being directly comparable.

useCases.LABEL: Coding
useCases.AXIS: Ordered on SWE-bench Verified where published, since it is the one coding benchmark most of these models report.

useCases.LABEL: Terminal & CLI work
useCases.AXIS: Terminal-Bench 2.1 only, so these are directly comparable. Models whose only published figure is on v2.0 are left out rather than mixed in - it is a different benchmark.

useCases.LABEL: Computer use (GUI)
useCases.AXIS: OSWorld and AndroidWorld, which are different suites - AndroidWorld figures are comparable to each other, OSWorld ones are not comparable to OSWorld-Verified. Only a handful of these models report computer-use numbers at all.

useCases.LABEL: Many parallel streams
useCases.AXIS: Ranked by active parameters and KV cost per token, because at concurrency those decide throughput far more than the benchmark scores do.

useCases.LABEL: Long context
useCases.AXIS: Ranked by KV bytes per token against the advertised ceiling - the models with a 1M window and latent attention are the only ones where a long context is affordable.

useCases.LABEL: Image generation
useCases.AXIS: No shared benchmark exists for these the way SWE-bench exists for coding, so this order is editorial: what the maintained runtime recommends, weighed against licence and footprint. The general-purpose models lead; below them are specialists worth jumping to for one job - readable text in the image, or training data with a clean licence.
RANK: 4B, edits as well as it generates
the one for readable text in the image

useCases.LABEL: Video generation
useCases.AXIS: Three entries, one runnable, and that is the story. Video is where Apple silicon is furthest behind - expect minutes per clip. MiniMax-H3 is the one most people use and the only one whose 8-bit build fits a single Mac at 21.5 GB resident, and LTX-2.5 is the better-quality newer release; both have MLX weights driven by standalone ports rather than any engine tracked here. LTX-2.3 is what MLX-Video actually loads.

useCases.LABEL: Voice agents (speech-to-speech)
useCases.AXIS: End-to-end speech models, where the model hears and speaks directly rather than being wired between an ASR and a TTS.

useCases.LABEL: Narration & text-to-speech
useCases.AXIS: Ordered on breadth of published MLX builds and language coverage; no common quality benchmark is published for these.

useCases.LABEL: Music generation
useCases.AXIS: Song generation from lyrics. One maintained MLX path.

51.headline: Add support for LTX-2.5
51.why: LTX-2.5 is the current Lightricks video model and MLX weights for it are already published, but mlx-video only implements LTX-2 and LTX-2.3. Until this lands, the newest weights have no loader in this engine.

805.headline: Disk KV cache can be reused across different weights sharing a model_id
805.why: Swap quantisations and the cache from the old weights can be restored against the new ones. Silent wrong-context, and it survives a restart because that is what the disk cache is for.

807.headline: DeepSeek V4 PRO 0813 support
807.why: The 0813 refresh is not yet a supported checkpoint. ds4 is deliberately narrow, so a newer PRO release is a tracked task rather than something that just loads.

816.headline: Stateless chat clients never extend the live KV session on Flash/Metal
816.why: Most agent clients are stateless - they resend a longer prompt each turn. If the session is not extended, the disk KV cache and prefix reuse stop paying, which is the main reason to run ds4.

836.headline: Possible ds4-server memory leak
836.why: Unconfirmed. On a machine where the model already occupies most of RAM, a slow server-side leak ends as an OOM rather than as swap.

839.headline: No tagged releases, which blocks downstream packaging
839.why: You build from a moving main branch. The project describes itself as beta and fast-changing, so pin a commit yourself if you care about reproducibility.

845.headline: --layers maps a shard as N disjoint Metal buffers, about 77x slower decode
845.why: Hits the distributed path specifically. If you are splitting DeepSeek V4 PRO or GLM-5.2 across two Macs, this is the first thing to check when the numbers look impossible.

851.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash vision is not supported
851.why: Text only today. Irrelevant for coding and terminal work; relevant if you wanted the same engine for screenshots.

853.headline: BPE merge loop is O(n squared): large prompts take minutes to tokenize
853.why: Tokenization is pure fixed cost before any GPU work. An agent that pastes a file into the prompt pays it on every turn, and it does not show up in the tok/s figures.

860.headline: ds4 crashes the machine on launch for one reporter
860.why: A single report without a resolved cause. Listed because a full-machine crash is a different risk class from a process crash.

27742.headline: model: add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp)
27742.why: Merged 2026-08-27, which is what unblocked this architecture. It is on master only - no tagged release carries it yet, so a packaged build will not load the weights until the next release cuts.

27752.headline: model: add GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5next)
27752.why: One of three competing open PRs for the same architecture (#27752, #27754, #27773). Quants are already published, so the weights are waiting on whichever of these lands.

25522.headline: Gemma 4 crashes with MTP speculative decoding
25522.why: MTP is the reason to prefer the GGUF build - the checkpoint ships a draft head. With MTP off the model runs, so this costs speed rather than correctness.

25739.headline: Google's own Gemma 4 QAT GGUF aborts at vocab load
25739.why: Closed 2026-09-03 as not planned, which is a decision not to fix rather than a fix - the vocab assert on Google's own QAT GGUF still stands. Filed against the E2B variant, and it matters because the QAT repo is the recommended download, so this is the default path and not an exotic one. Treat the closed marker as 'no longer being worked on'.

25751.headline: Sliding-window attention on Gemma 4 forgets key details
25751.why: Gemma 4's long context is built on SWA, so this bites exactly where the 256k window is the reason you picked the model. Quality loss, not a crash, which makes it harder to notice.

25967.headline: Duplicate GBNF rules with a large tool list break grammar parsing
25967.why: Closed 2026-09-03 as not planned - a decision not to fix rather than a fix, so the defect stands. Constrained decoding is how tool calls are kept well-formed, and past some number of tools the generated grammar fails to parse, which is to say the failure arrives exactly when an agent has enough tools to be useful. Read the closed marker as 'no longer being worked on'.

26365.headline: Kimi K3 full-size vision lives on a branch, not master
26365.why: Closed 2026-09-14 as not planned - a decision not to merge rather than a fix, so the situation stands: full-size Kimi K3 vision lives on a branch and mainline does not carry it. If you want vision on this model you are building someone's fork.

26382.headline: Same K and V cache type enforced for models with no V cache
26382.why: GLM-5.2's DSA attention has no V cache to quantise, but the flag pair is validated as if it did, so you cannot set the K type independently. Costs memory on the model that has the least to spare.

26894.headline: DFlash drafter fails to bind when the GGUF encodes attention.sliding_window
26894.why: Blocks speculative decoding on exactly the builds that carry a sliding-window key. The target model still runs; you lose the draft head's speedup.

27066.headline: Adaptive-P sampling is broken on Muse Glimmer
27066.why: A sampler, not the model. Pin top-p explicitly and it is a non-issue; listed because the default sampler config is what most launchers use.

27139.headline: Qwen3.8 tool-calling errors resolved by substituting the Qwen3.6 chat template
27139.why: The shipped template mis-renders something in the tool path. A workaround exists and is a single `--chat-template-file`, but until it is fixed the default template is wrong for agent use.

27141.headline: nemotron_h_moe aborts in ggml_ssm_scan during context reservation
27141.why: Fires at context reservation, before any token is generated, and the assertion is in the shared SSM scan rather than a backend - so it is not a CUDA-only report.

27335.headline: Qwen3.8-27B crashes on an M2 Ultra with default settings
27335.why: Confirmed on Darwin arm64 with the Metal backend, and on defaults rather than a tuned command line - the one class of bug that hits you on first run.

27427.headline: A ~50 KB request crashes llama-server with exit 139
27427.why: Filed on Glimmer. 50 KB is an ordinary agent turn once a file or a diff is in the prompt, and the process dies rather than rejecting the request.

27428.headline: draft-mtp roughly halves prompt processing on a multi-GPU layer split
27428.why: Multi-GPU only - a single GPU is fine, so this does not apply to a Mac. Listed because it is the most active MTP thread and the fix will touch the shared path.

27720.headline: gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel headers break tool calls
27720.why: gpt-oss encodes reasoning and tool calls in Harmony channels; a garbled header drops the call. Model specific and parser-side, so it is fixable without touching the weights.

27727.headline: Garbled output from a Qwen3-Coder-Next abliterated GGUF
27727.why: Filed against a community abliterated finetune rather than the base weights, so it may say more about that conversion than about the architecture. Worth knowing before you blame the model.

27741.headline: Feature request: support Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
27741.why: The request thread, still open even though the implementing PR (#27742) merged on 2026-08-27. Worth watching for the follow-up fixes rather than as a blocker; the remaining gap for this model is MLX, not llama.cpp.

3293.headline: Qwen4-Exp sparse-attention indexer fails under multi-row batching
3293.why: Fixed on 2026-09-02, but after v0.6.4 shipped and there has been no release since, so a packaged install still fails on any two concurrent requests. It was a shape error from the sparse-attention indexer that only appeared once continuous batching formed a multi-row batch - which is the configuration anyone serving this model would run.

3294.headline: Qwen4-Exp QSA cache: prefix blocks unusable across text and MRoPE turns
3294.why: Four defects in the QSA cache handling vendored in for Qwen4-Exp between v0.6.3rc3 and v0.6.3. Prefix cache reuse is the difference between a fast second turn and paying full prefill again, so this costs exactly what the engine is fastest at.

3300.headline: Loading another Qwen3.5-family VLM permanently breaks qwen4_exp Lightning MTP
3300.why: Fixed on 2026-08-30, and likewise not in a tagged release yet. Loading any other Qwen3.5-family VLM used to kill Lightning MTP for an already-working Flash-Next until restart, silently costing the 2.3x to 2.6x that MTP is worth on generation.

3303.headline: v0.6.4 qwen4-exp performance benchmark returns N/A for some prompt sizes
3303.why: The built-in benchmark intermittently reports nothing at pp16384. A reporting defect rather than an inference one, but it undercuts the numbers you would use to size a machine.

1195.headline: MTP speculative decoding not yet supported for Nemotron-H
1195.why: A feature request. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning ships MTP weights, so this is speed left on the table rather than anything broken.

1783.headline: Continuous batching prefill collapses at exactly two concurrent requests
1783.why: Recovers at higher concurrency, which makes it easy to miss in a benchmark that jumps straight to eight. Two concurrent requests is the most common real case.

1794.headline: Hitting the context wall with Gemma 4
1794.why: Gemma 4 advertises 256k. This is where users find the practical ceiling on a Mac, which is set by KV residency rather than by the model.

1862.headline: MiniMax 3 model-type error
1862.why: The `minimax_m3_vl` model type is not mapped cleanly. Same root cause as the loader failure above, seen from the config side.

1927.headline: GLM-5.2-mxfp4 will not load
1927.why: Filed against 0.4.4. Matters because mxfp4 is the smallest faithful GLM-5.2 build, and the alternative affine quants are larger at the same nominal bit width.

1968.headline: MiniMax-M3 fails to load: 2225 parameters not in model (vision_tower)
1968.why: The released checkpoint is `minimax_m3_vl` - a vision-language model - and the text path rejects the vision tower's tensors instead of skipping them.

2018.headline: OpenAI endpoint returns 500 while the Anthropic endpoint works
2018.why: Both endpoints front the same engine, so a client that speaks Anthropic gets a working server and a client that speaks OpenAI does not. Worth knowing which one your agent uses.

2099.headline: GLM-5.2 loops
2099.why: Repetition loops on the flagship model. A loop burns the context window and the wall clock without producing a turn, which on a metered agent is worse than an error.

2137.headline: GLM-5.2-mxfp4 prefill fell from 160-180 tok/s to 40 tok/s on 0.5.0.dev2
2137.why: Closed as completed in July 2026, with memory also fluctuating between 400 and 520 GB on a 512 GB M3 Ultra. Kept on the list as the reference point for what a healthy GLM-5.2 prefill looks like, and as a reminder that a version bump can cost you a factor of four on this model.

2208.headline: GLM-5.2 cold prefill throttles near the memory ceiling
2208.why: GLM-5.2 leaves very little headroom on any Mac that can hold it, so the adaptive throttle engages in normal use rather than at an extreme.

2216.headline: Legitimate gpt-oss tool calls with explicit to=functions.* are dropped
2216.why: A regression from a stricter channel check. Calls that are correctly formed per the Harmony spec get discarded, so the agent sees a turn with no action.

2252.headline: A broken-load DFlash helper poisons concurrent requests to an unrelated model
2252.why: Cross-contamination between models in the same server, on the Qwen3-Next batched path specifically.

2307.headline: A model-discovery race orphans a loaded engine - 404 GB unreclaimable, restart only
2307.why: Server-wide, not per model. Discovery racing an in-flight load leaks the whole resident model; on a 256 GB machine that is the entire budget gone until you restart.

2469.headline: DeepSeek V4 mxfp4 gather_qmm_blocks crashes on float32 activations
2469.why: MXFP4 is the quantisation DeepSeek actually released, so this is the preferred build rather than a fringe one.

2493.headline: 'Cache signature mismatch' then a severe performance drop on DeepSeek V4
2493.why: The prefix cache silently stops being used, so every turn re-prefills. On long agent conversations that is the difference between seconds and minutes per turn.

2589.headline: Muse Glimmer oQ4e: tool calling broken and decode slow
2589.why: Tool calling is the whole point of Glimmer - it leads MCP Atlas. Traced to a pre-#1839 quantisation, so check which build you pulled before concluding the model is bad.

2590.headline: Scope clarification: MiniMax M3 long-prefill fixes across Q4 and oQ3
2590.why: An open question about which quant tiers the long-prefill fixes cover. Read it before choosing a MiniMax quant, because the answer decides whether long prompts work.

2600.headline: DFlash speculative decoding renders the cache non-functional on Gemma and Glimmer
2600.why: Turning on the draft head disables the prefix cache, so you trade a decode speedup for full re-prefill every turn. On agent workloads that is a net loss.

2604.headline: Glimmer DFlash can end a turn after reasoning without the forced tool call
2604.why: The model finishes its reasoning and stops instead of emitting the call. An agent sees a turn that did nothing, which usually gets retried - so it costs two turns, not one.

2606.headline: Thinking leaks into content when generation is truncated mid-thought
2606.why: A truncated turn returns reasoning as if it were the answer. Downstream that is indistinguishable from the model answering badly, and it corrupts anything that parses the reply.

2641.headline: Glimmer is extremely slow with DFlash on
2641.why: The companion report to the two above: on this family the draft head currently costs more than it saves. Run Glimmer without it.

2691.headline: Request: an oQ4e-mtp quantisation of Qwen3.8-27B
2691.why: oMLX's own quant format with the MTP head merged. Until it exists you are running a generic mlx-community build rather than one tuned for this server.

2747.headline: Qwen3.8-27B single-stream decode regressed 36.5 to 24 tok/s on an M3 Ultra
2747.why: A third of decode throughput, on the model most people will try first, with the MTP path implicated. This is the number to check against before assuming an MLX server beats llama.cpp here.

2786.headline: Gemma 4 performance regressed after 0.6.1
2786.why: A version-pinning matter rather than an architecture one, but it means the newest build is not automatically the right one for this model.

2854.headline: No continuous-batching results published for Qwen3.8 and DFlash2
2854.why: Continuous batching is the reason to run a server instead of the CLI. Unmeasured on this architecture means the concurrency story is unproven, not that it is broken.

2972.headline: Process-global Qwen patches contaminate a resident engine after loading another model
2972.why: Multi-model serving is a headline oMLX feature; this is the cross-contamination it can cause. The second model loads and the first one quietly changes behaviour.

3006.headline: GLM-5.2 prefill far below published figures on an M3 Ultra 512 GB
3006.why: The published 845 tok/s number depends on the native DSA kernels being compiled in. This thread is where you find out whether your install actually has them - the fallback is roughly 30x slower and uses more memory.

3117.headline: Qwen3.8 with the Neural Engine enabled produces zero tokens
3117.why: ANE offload is off by default, so this is an opt-in trap rather than a first-run one - but it is silent, returning an empty completion rather than an error.

3121.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash decodes at 4-17 tok/s on an M5 Max from residency thrash
3121.why: Closed as completed on 2026-08-28, alongside the v0.6.3 release. It was traced to the bundled mlx keeping a single residency set, so weights faulted instead of staying wired. No post-fix decode figure has been published, so treat the old 4-17 tok/s as historical rather than current - and the other DeepSeek defects on this engine are still open.

2240.headline: Too much memory allocated
2240.why: Over-allocation relative to the model. On a 256 GB machine running a 200 GB model there is no slack to absorb it.

2243.headline: Native MLX tool calling: parser coverage requests
2243.why: Tool-call parsing is per-family, so a model whose format has no parser returns its calls as text. Track this if your model is not in the supported list.

2265.headline: MLX Gemma 4 silently ignores attached images and confabulates a description
2265.why: The GGUF build of the same model handles them. A vision model that invents what it cannot see is the worst available failure mode, and it is engine-specific.

2273.headline: MLX quants shown as having no tool use when they do
2273.why: The capability badge is wrong, so the app steers you away from working tool-calling builds. Cosmetic in code, decision-changing in practice.

2323.headline: MLX engine silently clamps context to 4864 tokens, ignoring all overrides
2323.why: Filed against a hybrid linear-attention model - the Qwen3.8 shape. A silent 4864-token ceiling makes any agent workload fail in a way that looks like the model being stupid rather than the engine being misconfigured.

2324.headline: Catalog entries show 'Invalid Key ID' with no download options
2324.why: A catalogue-side failure rather than an inference one, but the catalogue is how most people get models into this app.

1788.headline: Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) model support
1788.why: Open. Until it merges mlx-lm has no qwen4_exp class, so every MLX engine that builds on mlx-lm refuses the weights regardless of which quant you point at it.

1162.headline: Qwen3-Next hybrid cache silently fails, breaking the prompt cache
1162.why: Silent, and it removes prefix reuse - the single biggest win on multi-turn agent traffic. Every MLX server that wraps mlx-lm inherits it, so the model looks fine while every turn re-prefills.

1192.headline: The DeepSeek V4 port thread
1192.why: Where the community port was developed and tested before PR #1233. Useful for finding out what already works in a fork if you do not want to wait for the merge.

1233.headline: PR: DeepSeek V4 model class, still open
1233.why: This is the entire MLX blocker for DeepSeek V4. Until it merges there is no `deepseek_v4` in mlx-lm, so no MLX server that wraps mlx-lm can load the architecture no matter which quant you download.

1242.headline: Error loading mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit
1242.why: The published small-variant quant does not load cleanly.

1281.headline: Request: add DeepSeek V4 to mlx_lm
1281.why: The demand-side thread for the PR above. Useful as a temperature check on whether the port is moving.

1332.headline: DeepSeek-V4 unbounded Metal residency during decode
1332.why: Dies at ~11k decode tokens with metal::malloc resource-limit exceeded. Even once the architecture lands, this has to be fixed before the model is servable.

1335.headline: Tool calls dropped when the tokenizer merges the tool-call start marker
1335.why: The json_tools parser never matches, so the call is returned as plain text. Architecture-independent and specific to agent use.

1352.headline: Gemma 4 with thinking enabled returns only reasoning, content empty
1352.why: The visible reply comes back blank whenever thinking is on.

1401.headline: PR: Add MiniMax-M3 (text backbone) - unmerged
1401.why: The only route to M3 on MLX, open since 2026-08-24. The only route to M3 on MLX.

1404.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash drifts from Simplified to Traditional Chinese
1404.why: Filed against the mlx-vlm DeepSeek path, which is the only working MLX route today. A quality defect rather than a load failure, and confined to CJK output.

1418.headline: GLM-5.2 fails to load — missing per-layer indexer params
1418.why: The loader expects a DeepSeek-V3.2-style indexer on every layer, but GLM-5.2's IndexShare places them on a subset. mlx-community/GLM-5.2-mxfp4 aborts with 285 missing parameters.

1443.headline: DSA Indexer sparse top-k evicts attention sinks
1443.why: Past index_topk (2048) the indexer drops the attention sinks and decode collapses into repetition — a sharp cliff, not drift. Hits every sparse-attention model: DeepSeek V3.2/V4 and GLM-5.2 both decode through this module.

1446.headline: ArraysCache is not trimmable
1446.why: The structural reason the k=1 cap exists — GDN state layers cannot be rolled back on draft rejection. Same root cause as #730.

1493.headline: Generation hangs at 0% CPU right after prompt processing
1493.why: A wedge, not a slowdown - the server stops doing work with no error.

1572.headline: >300GB models trip the GPU watchdog at load
1572.why: load_model() ends with one mx.eval(model.parameters()), building a single enormous Metal command buffer. At ~390GB it hits kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout and the error escapes uncaught, hard-aborting the process. GLM-5.2 at 4-bit is 372-475GB.

1573.headline: RotatingKVCache.to_quantized() blocks --kv-bits on sliding-window layers
1573.why: Gemma 4's sliding-window attention cannot use a quantised KV cache.

1662.headline: Models that discard update_and_fetch's return leak one Metal buffer per layer per generation
1662.why: Fixed upstream. #1784 makes decode evaluate cache state periodically and #1790 fixes the unevaluated graph in deepseek specifically; both merged, and this closed 2026-08-27. It was the general form of the DeepSeek V4 residency growth - any model class written that way leaked for the life of the process, aborting at around 11k generated tokens rather than failing on the first run.

14116.headline: Tiered context length can exhaust VRAM
14116.why: Fixed, closed 2026-09-04. The automatic context sizing could commit more memory than the machine had, and on a Mac that is unified memory, so it took the whole machine rather than just a GPU. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

15813.headline: Metal backend crash on Apple M5: bfloat/half type mismatch
15813.why: An M5-specific crash in the Metal matmul path. If you are buying an M5 machine, this is the one to check is closed before you plan around Ollama on it.

17323.headline: Bare-JSON tool-call models silently drop content generated after the call
17323.why: The call survives and the accompanying text does not. Silent truncation is worse than an error because the agent proceeds on a partial turn.

17569.headline: x/mlxrunner panics importing a plain Qwen3 MLX 4-bit model
17569.why: An index-out-of-range in the MLX runner's dense MLP forward. Importing an ordinary mlx-community checkpoint is a normal thing to want to do.

17638.headline: gpt-oss: HTTP 500 'error parsing tool call' on a call its own model generated
17638.why: The server rejects output produced by the model it shipped. From the agent's side it is a hard failure on a turn that was otherwise correct.

17656.headline: muse-glimmer:30b-mlx is built from nvfp4-dflash layers, not real MLX weights
17656.why: The tag says MLX and the manifest says something else, so you may not be running what you think you are. Worth knowing generally: an Ollama tag is a manifest, not a guarantee about the underlying build.

17776.headline: Qwen3.8-27B MTP variants are 2x slower than non-MTP on Apple Silicon
17776.why: Speculative decoding making decode twice as slow is the opposite of the intent. On this model MTP is the main reason to prefer one engine over another, so a negative result here matters.

17783.headline: gemma4:31b-mlx grows in memory over a session
17783.why: Fixed, closed 2026-09-10. Resident size climbed across a session on the MLX path, which matters most on a machine sized close to the model - the failure arrives after hours rather than at load. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

17878.headline: Embeddings silently return all-zero vectors under sustained load
17878.why: HTTP 200, plausible usage numbers, and useless vectors. Not an LLM path, but it says something about how failures surface here.

360.headline: RFC: a specialised Metal kernel for MLA paged attention
360.why: Until this exists, latent-attention models fall back to MLX SDPA with no Metal kernel - which is why the GLM-4.5 row in the support matrix is flagged as slow and untested.

450.headline: RFC: attention backend dispatch
450.why: Design work on how backends get selected per model. Useful for judging how settled the internals are.

482.headline: Draft-model speculative decoding is net-negative
482.why: Each request re-ingests the full prompt into the draft model, which costs more than the draft saves. Worth knowing before you reach for spec decode here; the built-in MTP path (#610) is the one to watch.

610.headline: Built-in MTP draft heads do not yet work with prefix caching on hybrid GDN
610.why: Qwen3.8 is exactly that shape, and it ships an MTP head. Until this lands you choose between the draft head and the prefix cache rather than having both.

644.headline: Nemotron-H (Mamba-2 + MoE hybrid) paged attention not implemented
644.why: Closed as completed on 2026-09-09 after a long chain of work - hybrid geometry behind a family owner, a state-family routing table, Mamba-2 mixers on paged state, and finally Nemotron-H through the decode pipeline. Kept listed because the fix is nightly-only: the v0.28.0 stable predates it. Before this, such a model loaded, warmed up, reported healthy and then killed EngineCore on the first request.

646.headline: Mixed batches with top_k enabled on some requests crash the Metal sampler
646.why: Fixed. PR #648 normalises disabled top_k rows to vocab_size and merged 2026-08-27, closing this. It mattered because continuous batching puts requests with different sampling parameters in one batch, so it was reachable with ordinary mixed traffic. Kept listed so the fix is dated: you want a build from 2026-08-27 or later.

546.headline: Strict json_schema decode wedges with no token progress
546.why: Over 5-minute hangs on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B. Structured output is load-bearing for tool arguments.

570.headline: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B dequantize shape mismatch (works in mlx-vlm)
570.why: Same class as mlx-lm #1197: mlx-vlm handles a checkpoint the mlx-lm path does not.

584.headline: Non-loopback requests silently dropped on --host 0.0.0.0
584.why: Deployment blocker: a server on the LAN is reachable only from localhost. Silent — no log, recv-queue 0.

590.headline: Gemma 4 TextModel dispatch, logit_bias API, and MLLM fallback stalls
590.why: Dispatch falls through to qwen3_5 rather than the Gemma path.

619.headline: Hardcoded mx.set_cache_limit(32GB) is not device-scaled
619.why: Filed as an OOM on small Macs, but it cuts the other way here: a hardcoded 32GB ceiling on a 256GB box leaves most of the machine unused.

627.headline: memory_budget_gb never reconciled with the Metal allocation ceiling
627.why: Two allocators with different ideas of the budget. Relevant when hot-swapping checkpoints for A/B runs.

641.headline: MemoryAwarePrefixCache stores caches by reference
641.why: Leaks Metal buffer handles on hybrid models. Compounds every other memory-pressure item at concurrency.

658.headline: Validate Qwen MoE MTP conversion artifacts before decode
658.why: Would catch a broken MTP head at load instead of at generation.

668.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash unsupported
668.why: ValueError: Model type deepseek_v4 not supported. Open since 2026-08-01, no maintainer reply, no PR — and mlx-lm has no deepseek_v4.py, so the architecture is unimplemented upstream too.

672.headline: Streaming tool calls can end without finish_reason
672.why: Fixed, closed 2026-08-30. It mattered because a streaming tool call that ends without a terminator is exactly the shape that reads as a fabricated turn downstream. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

678.headline: Prefix cache trims RotatingKVCache past its window
678.why: Cross-conversation KV leak and repetition loops. A correctness bug, not a speed bug — one tenant's context bleeding into another's is disqualifying for multi-agent serving.

682.headline: Closing a stream leaves the inner generator and request state open
682.why: Client disconnects are routine in agentic work; leaked request state accumulates.

689.headline: Completion cache can store desynchronized rotating KV state
689.why: Another way the cache serves state that does not match the prompt it is keyed on.

699.headline: DFlash and DSpark draft heads block speculative decoding
699.why: Both are the vendor-shipped draft mechanisms on the models that have one. If neither is wired up, speculative decoding on this engine is limited to what the generic k=1 path gives you.

710.headline: MTP drafting pinned to k=1 on hybrid linear-attention
710.why: Reference CUDA/vLLM deployments run k=3 at ~77% acceptance for a ~66% decode gain. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B / M3 Ultra 256GB: verify forward is 69% of step time, reject and replay 19.3%.

711.headline: --prefill-step-size silently dropped under --continuous-batching
711.why: Prefill chunk size is the main Apple Silicon prefill lever, ignored in exactly the config we would run.

725.headline: PR: GLM-4.7 thinking streams into content, not reasoning_content
725.why: With --reasoning-parser glm4 the entire thinking block lands in content. Non-streaming is unaffected, so it is easy to miss - an agent frontend renders the model's reasoning as the visible reply.

729.headline: PR: honor --prefill-step-size with continuous batching
729.why: Merged 2026-09-04. It was one of two competing fixes for #711; this is the one that landed, making --prefill-step-size actually apply under continuous batching.

730.headline: Prefix-cache reuse silently disabled for hybrid architectures
730.why: #691's all-or-nothing rewind gate rejects every hybrid model: ArraysCache leaves have no .keys and inherit is_trimmable() -> False. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B-8bit — an identical 24k prompt resent back-to-back gives zero speedup on main, versus ~58x before #691. Rejection logs only at DEBUG.
